API reference

Simulation setup and control

physicellpy.initialize(config_path: str, mechanics_voxel_size: float = 30.0) → None

Load a PhysiCell_settings.xml config and run the standard startup sequence (microenvironment + default cell-function assignment + cell definitions + signal/behavior dictionaries + cell rules + cell container). Call this once before create_cell(). Does NOT place any initial cells – call setup_tissue() for the generic case, or place cells yourself.

physicellpy.setup_tissue() → None

Generic initial-tissue-placement helper: places parameters.ints(‘number_of_cells’) cells of every registered cell type at random positions across the domain (skipped if that int parameter isn’t defined in the config), then loads any CSV-specified cells and applies <initial_parameter_distributions> from the config. Unlike a sample project’s own setup_tissue(), this doesn’t reference any cell type by name.

physicellpy.run_simulation_step() → None

Advance the simulation by one diffusion_dt: diffusion/decay, cell mechanics/phenotype update, backfill Python hooks onto any new daughter cells (see sync_cell_hooks()), then current_time += diffusion_dt. Call this from a Python loop to actually step the simulation forward.

physicellpy.sync_cell_hooks() → None

Backfill Python phenotype hooks (registered via CellDefinition.set_update_phenotype() etc.) onto daughter cells created by division since the last call. run_simulation_step() already calls this automatically every step, so you normally don’t need to call it yourself – kept as a standalone function for callers advancing time some other way.

physicellpy.current_time() → float

Current simulation time (minutes), as advanced by run_simulation_step()

physicellpy.max_time() → float

Simulation end time (minutes) from the loaded config’s <max_time>

physicellpy.diffusion_dt() → float

Diffusion time step (minutes) from the loaded config’s <dt_diffusion>

physicellpy.mechanics_dt() → float

Mechanics time step (minutes) from the loaded config’s <dt_mechanics> – a distinct value from diffusion_dt(). Needed for pc.physimess_mechanics(dt), which expects the same dt PhysiCell’s own main.cpp passes it (PhysiMeSS.cpp self-gates on this value, same pattern update_all_cells() uses internally for its own mechanics/phenotype timing).

physicellpy.simulate_2D() → bool

Whether the loaded config’s domain is 2D (<use_2D> in <options>) – the Z coordinate should be pinned to 0 when placing cells if so, matching every sample project’s own setup_tissue().

physicellpy.config_folder() → str

Output folder as set by the loaded config’s <save><folder> option

physicellpy.load_cells_from_pugixml() → None

Place any cells specified by <initial_conditions><cell_positions> in the loaded config (e.g. from a CSV file). setup_tissue() already calls this; call it directly only if you’re writing your own setup_tissue() replacement in Python and still want config-driven cell placement layered on top.

class physicellpy.UserParameters

Cells and cell types

physicellpy.create_cell(arg0: physicellpy.CellDefinition) → physicellpy.Cell

Create a new cell from a Cell_Definition; ownership stays with PhysiCell

physicellpy.delete_cell(arg0: physicellpy.Cell) → None

Mark a cell for deletion via PhysiCell’s own bookkeeping

physicellpy.all_cells() → list[physicellpy.Cell]

Access the global list of all cells currently in the simulation

physicellpy.find_cell_definition(arg0: str) → physicellpy.CellDefinition

Look up an already-registered Cell_Definition by name (live reference, not a copy)

physicellpy.cell_type_names() → list[str]

List the names of all registered cell types (populated by pc.initialize())

physicellpy.register_cell_definition(arg0: physicellpy.CellDefinition) → None

Register a CellDefinition built via pc.CellDefinition(other_def) so it becomes findable via find_cell_definition() and appears in cell_type_names(). Set a unique .name (and .type, e.g. len(pc.cell_type_names())) first.

class physicellpy.Cell
property ID

This cell’s unique integer ID, assigned at creation

clear_contact_function(self: physicellpy.Cell) → None

Unregister the per-cell contact_function hook set by set_contact_function()

clear_custom_cell_rule(self: physicellpy.Cell) → None

Unregister the per-cell custom_cell_rule hook set by set_custom_cell_rule()

clear_update_phenotype(self: physicellpy.Cell) → None

Unregister the per-cell update_phenotype hook set by set_update_phenotype()

property custom_data

X’ signals

Type:

This cell’s CustomCellData – the grammar’s ‘custom

flag_for_division(self: physicellpy.Cell) → None

Mark this cell for division at the next mechanics update

flag_for_removal(self: physicellpy.Cell) → None

Mark this cell for removal at the next mechanics update

is_out_of_domain(self: physicellpy.Cell) → bool

Whether the cell has moved outside the simulation domain

nearest_density_vector(self: physicellpy.Cell) → numpy.ndarray[numpy.float64]

Zero-copy view of the local substrate concentrations at this cell’s voxel

property orientation

Unit vector describing this cell/fibre’s orientation (used by PhysiMeSS fibres; generally unused for ordinary cells)

property parameters

This cell’s CellParameters (O2-response thresholds)

property phenotype

This cell’s live Phenotype

property position

[x, y, z] position (micron). Setting this re-indexes the cell into the correct mechanics voxel, unlike writing c.position[i] in place.

set_contact_function(self: physicellpy.Cell, arg0: Callable) → None

Register a Python callable contact_function(cell, phenotype, other_cell, other_phenotype, dt) hook for this cell only.

set_custom_cell_rule(self: physicellpy.Cell, arg0: Callable) → None

Register a Python callable custom_cell_rule(cell, phenotype, dt) hook for this cell only.

set_internal_uptake_constants(self: physicellpy.Cell, arg0: float) → None

Recompute internal secretion/uptake constants from the cell’s current volume and rates. Call this after changing phenotype.volume or phenotype.secretion’s rates, with the same dt as your diffusion step.

set_total_volume(self: physicellpy.Cell, arg0: float) → None

Set phenotype.volume.total, splitting the new value proportionally across nuclear/cytoplasmic/fluid components

set_update_phenotype(self: physicellpy.Cell, arg0: Callable) → None

Register a Python callable update_phenotype(cell, phenotype, dt) hook for this cell only.

property simple_pressure

Nondimensionalized mechanical pressure acting on the cell – the grammar’s ‘pressure’ signal (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf)

property type

This cell’s integer type index

property type_name

This cell’s type name – used by the ‘contact with Y’ family of signals

update_position(self: physicellpy.Cell, arg0: float) → None

Integrate position forward by dt using the cell’s current velocity

property velocity

Current [vx, vy, vz] velocity (micron/min), from adhesion/repulsion/motility

class physicellpy.CellDefinition
clear_contact_function(self: physicellpy.CellDefinition) → None

Unregister the contact_function hook set by set_contact_function()

clear_custom_cell_rule(self: physicellpy.CellDefinition) → None

Unregister the custom_cell_rule hook set by set_custom_cell_rule()

clear_update_phenotype(self: physicellpy.CellDefinition) → None

Unregister the update_phenotype hook set by set_update_phenotype()

property custom_data

This cell type’s default CustomCellData – copied onto every new cell created from this definition

property name

This cell type’s name, e.g. ‘macrophage’ – how it’s referred to in rules/config files and by find_cell_definition()

property parameters

This cell type’s CellParameters (O2-response thresholds for the standard O2-based phenotype model)

property phenotype

The template Phenotype every new create_cell() call against this definition copies its starting values from

set_contact_function(self: physicellpy.CellDefinition, arg0: Callable) → None

Register a Python callable contact_function(cell, phenotype, other_cell, other_phenotype, dt) hook, called for each spring-attached neighbor. Applied to every future create_cell() call against this definition.

set_custom_cell_rule(self: physicellpy.CellDefinition, arg0: Callable) → None

Register a Python callable custom_cell_rule(cell, phenotype, dt) hook, applied to every future create_cell() call against this definition.

set_update_phenotype(self: physicellpy.CellDefinition, arg0: Callable) → None

Register a Python callable update_phenotype(cell, phenotype, dt) hook, applied to every future create_cell() call against this definition.

property type

This cell type’s integer index (must be unique; see register_cell_definition())

class physicellpy.CellParameters
class physicellpy.CustomCellData
variables(self: physicellpy.CustomCellData) → list[str]

List the names of every custom variable defined on this cell/definition

Phenotype and the behavior grammar

Field/method docstrings in this section cite the reference (or recommended) parameter values from Cell_grammar_supp.pdf’s behavior dictionary tables directly, so a docstring here doubles as a quick reference for reasonable default magnitudes.

class physicellpy.Phenotype
property cell_integrity

This cell’s CellIntegrity sub-object – accumulated damage/repair

property cell_interactions

This cell’s CellInteractions sub-object – phagocytosis/attack/fusion

property cell_transformations

This cell’s CellTransformations sub-object – spontaneous type-change rates

property death

This cell’s Death sub-object – apoptosis/necrosis state

property flagged_for_division

Set True to mark this cell for division at the next mechanics update

property flagged_for_removal

Set True to mark this cell for removal at the next mechanics update

property geometry

This cell’s Geometry sub-object (radius, etc.)

property mechanics

This cell’s Mechanics sub-object – cell-cell adhesion/repulsion

property motility

This cell’s Motility sub-object – migration speed/bias/persistence

property secretion

This cell’s Secretion sub-object – per-substrate secretion/uptake/export

property volume

This cell’s Volume sub-object

class physicellpy.Volume
property cytoplasmic

Cytoplasmic volume (micron^3)

property cytoplasmic_biomass_change_rate

Rate (1/min) the cytoplasmic solid volume relaxes toward its target

divide(self: physicellpy.Volume) → None

Halve every volume component – called on both daughter cells at division

property fluid_fraction

Fraction of total volume that is fluid (dimensionless, 0-1)

multiply_by_ratio(self: physicellpy.Volume, arg0: float) → None

Scale every volume component by a common factor

property nuclear

Nuclear volume (micron^3)

property nuclear_biomass_change_rate

Rate (1/min) the nuclear solid volume relaxes toward its target

property target_solid_cytoplasmic

Target solid cytoplasmic volume (micron^3) the cell grows/shrinks toward

property target_solid_nuclear

Target solid nuclear volume (micron^3) the cell grows/shrinks toward

property total

Total cell volume (micron^3) – the grammar’s ‘volume’ signal (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, List of signal terms)

class physicellpy.Geometry
class physicellpy.Mechanics
property cell_BM_adhesion_strength

Cell-basement-membrane adhesion strength – grammar symbol reserved for future reference models (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Other terms)

property cell_BM_repulsion_strength

Cell-basement-membrane repulsion strength – grammar symbol reserved for future reference models (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Other terms)

property cell_cell_adhesion_strength

Cell-cell adhesion coefficient alpha_i (micron/min) – the grammar’s ‘cell-cell adhesion’ behavior; reference value 0.4 micron/min (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Cell-cell adhesion and repulsion terms)

property cell_cell_repulsion_strength

Cell-cell repulsion coefficient beta_i (micron/min) – the grammar’s ‘cell-cell repulsion’ behavior, resisting deformation/overlap; reference value 10 micron/min

property relative_maximum_adhesion_distance

Maximum adhesion interaction distance R_A,i / R_i, as a multiple of the cell’s own radius – the grammar’s ‘relative maximum adhesion distance’ behavior; reference value 1.25 (sometimes increased to 1.5)

class physicellpy.Motility
property is_motile

Whether this cell moves at all (<motility><options><enabled> in the config)

property migration_bias

Migration bias b in [0,1] – 0 is unbiased (Brownian) motion, 1 is fully directed along migration_bias_direction; reference value 0.5

property migration_bias_direction

Unit vector d_bias the cell’s motility is biased toward (e.g. a chemotactic gradient direction)

property migration_speed

Migration speed s (micron/min) – the grammar’s ‘migration speed’ behavior; reference value 1 micron/min

property persistence_time

Migration persistence time T_persist (min) – mean time between re-randomizing the motility direction; reference value 5 min (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Migration terms)

class physicellpy.Death
check_for_death(self: physicellpy.Death, arg0: float) → bool

Stochastically test every registered death model’s rate (e.g. apoptosis d_A, necrosis d_N – Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Death terms) against dt and trigger one if it fires; returns True if this call triggered a death

property dead

Whether the cell is dead – the grammar’s ‘dead’ signal. Also see the ‘apoptotic’/’necrotic’ signals for which death model fired

trigger_death(self: physicellpy.Death, arg0: int) → None

Force this cell into the given death model index immediately (bypassing the stochastic rate check); see the note above on why this doesn’t cleanly reverse

class physicellpy.Secretion
advance(self: physicellpy.Secretion, cell: PhysiCell::Cell, phenotype: PhysiCell::Phenotype, dt: float) → None

Advance secretion/uptake for one cell by dt against its local voxel

net_export_rate(self: physicellpy.Secretion, arg0: str) → float

Net export rate for the named substrate (substrate/cell/min)

property net_export_rates

Per-substrate net export rates E_i (substrate/cell/min), for bulk export independent of the secretion/uptake reaction-diffusion form – the grammar’s ‘X export’ behavior; 0 by default

property saturation_densities

Per-substrate secretion target densities rho*_i – secretion slows as the local concentration approaches this value; the grammar’s ‘X secretion target’ behavior

saturation_density(self: physicellpy.Secretion, arg0: str) → float

Secretion target density for the named substrate

scale_all_secretion_by_factor(self: physicellpy.Secretion, arg0: float) → None

Multiply every substrate’s secretion_rate by a common factor

scale_all_uptake_by_factor(self: physicellpy.Secretion, arg0: float) → None

Multiply every substrate’s uptake_rate by a common factor

secretion_rate(self: physicellpy.Secretion, arg0: str) → float

Secretion rate for the named substrate (1/min)

property secretion_rates

Per-substrate secretion rates S_i (1/min), indexed like the microenvironment’s substrates – the grammar’s ‘X secretion’ behavior; 0 by default, 10 min^-1 recommended for secreting cells (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Secretion, uptake, and export terms)

set_all_secretion_to_zero(self: physicellpy.Secretion) → None

Zero out secretion_rates for every substrate

set_all_uptake_to_zero(self: physicellpy.Secretion) → None

Zero out uptake_rates for every substrate

set_secretion_rate(self: physicellpy.Secretion, arg0: str, arg1: float) → None

Set the secretion rate for the named substrate (1/min)

set_uptake_rate(self: physicellpy.Secretion, arg0: str, arg1: float) → None

Set the uptake rate for the named substrate (1/min)

uptake_rate(self: physicellpy.Secretion, arg0: str) → float

Uptake (consumption) rate for the named substrate (1/min)

property uptake_rates

Per-substrate uptake (consumption) rates U_i (1/min) – the grammar’s ‘X uptake’ behavior; 0 by default

class physicellpy.CellInteractions
property apoptotic_phagocytosis_rate

Rate r_PA,i (1/min) of phagocytosing apoptotic cells in contact – the grammar’s ‘phagocytose apoptotic cell’ behavior; reference value 0.1 min^-1 (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Key cell-cell interaction terms)

property attack_damage_rate
Type:

Damage inflicted per minute of attack, r_AD – reference value 1 min^-1 (dimensionless damage tracks total attack time 1

property attack_duration

Mean attack duration T_attack (min) before the attack ends; reference value 15 min for cytotoxic T cells; 0 by default

attack_rate(self: physicellpy.CellInteractions, arg0: str) → float

Rate of attacking live cells of the named type (1/min)

property attack_rates

Per-type rates r_A,ij (1/min) of initiating a cytotoxic attack on live cells of type j – the grammar’s ‘attack X’ behavior; 0 by default, 0.1 min^-1 recommended for cytotoxic T cells

property attack_target

The Cell this cell is currently attacking, or None

fusion_rate(self: physicellpy.CellInteractions, arg0: str) → float

Rate of fusing with contacted cells of the named type (1/min)

property fusion_rates

Per-type rates r_F,ij (1/min) of fusing with a contacted cell of type j – the grammar’s ‘fuse to X’ behavior; 0 by default, 0.03 min^-1 recommended for epithelial fusion

property immunogenicities

Per-type immunogenicity g_A,ij of this cell to an attacking cell of type j – the grammar’s ‘immunogenicity to X’ behavior; 1 by default

immunogenicity(self: physicellpy.CellInteractions, arg0: str) → float

This cell’s immunogenicity to an attacking cell of the named type

live_phagocytosis_rate(self: physicellpy.CellInteractions, arg0: str) → float

Rate of phagocytosing live cells of the named type (1/min)

property live_phagocytosis_rates

Per-type rates r_PL,ij (1/min) of phagocytosing live cells of type j – the grammar’s ‘phagocytose X’ behavior; 0 by default

property necrotic_phagocytosis_rate

Rate r_PN,i (1/min) of phagocytosing necrotic cells in contact – the grammar’s ‘phagocytose necrotic cell’ behavior; reference value 0.017 min^-1

property other_dead_phagocytosis_rate

Rate r_PO,i (1/min) of phagocytosing cells dead from any other model – the grammar’s ‘phagocytose other dead cell’ behavior; reference value 0.1 min^-1

set_attack_rate(self: physicellpy.CellInteractions, arg0: str, arg1: float) → None

Set the rate of attacking live cells of the named type (1/min)

property total_damage_delivered

Cumulative damage this (attacking) cell has delivered – the grammar’s ‘damage delivered’ signal

class physicellpy.CellTransformations
set_transformation_rate(self: physicellpy.CellTransformations, arg0: str, arg1: float) → None

Set the transformation rate to the named cell type (1/min)

transformation_rate(self: physicellpy.CellTransformations, arg0: str) → float

Transformation rate to the named cell type (1/min)

property transformation_rates

Per-type spontaneous transformation rates r_T,ij (1/min) – the grammar’s ‘transform to X’ behavior (differentiation, transdifferentiation, mutation); 0 by default for every type (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Cell Transition or Transformation)

class physicellpy.CellIntegrity
property damage

Accumulated (dimensionless) non-effector-attack damage – the grammar’s ‘damage’ signal, tracking e.g. cytotoxic drug/toxin exposure independent of effector-attack damage (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf, Cell Integrity)

property damage_rate

Rate r_damage (1/min) damage accumulates – the grammar’s ‘damage rate’ behavior; 0 by default, 1 min^-1 recommended when modeling damage

property damage_repair_rate

Exponential repair rate r_repair (1/min) damage decays at – the grammar’s ‘damage repair rate’ behavior; 0 by default, 0.012 min^-1 recommended for recovery from sublethal T cell attack

Behavior rules (Hypothesis_Rule grammar)

physicellpy.find_ruleset(arg0: physicellpy.CellDefinition) → physicellpy.HypothesisRuleset

The HypothesisRuleset for this cell type, or None if it has no rules at all (e.g. rules_enabled is false, or no rule in the loaded CSV/XML targets it).

physicellpy.read_rules(filename: str) → None

Parse an additional v3-format cell_rules.csv into the live ruleset, on top of whatever setup_cell_rules() already loaded from the config’s own <cell_rules> block. Cell types referenced by name in the file must already be registered (i.e. call this after initialize()). WARNING: re-parsing a rule that’s already present – same (cell_type, signal, behavior, response) – calls PhysiCell’s own exit(-1) directly (PhysiCell_rules.cpp), which kills the whole Python process immediately with no exception and no traceback – try/except cannot catch it. If your config’s own <cell_rules> already points at this same file, don’t call read_rules() on it again; use find_ruleset()/HypothesisRuleset.find_behavior() to inspect or edit the already-loaded rules instead.

physicellpy.add_rule(cell_type: str, signal: str, behavior: str, response: str, use_for_dead: object = None) → None

Add a new rule from Python, e.g. add_rule(‘villager’, ‘contact with zombie’, ‘transform to zombie’, ‘increases’). response is ‘increases’ or ‘decreases’. WARNING: adding a (cell_type, signal, behavior, response) that already exists kills the whole Python process instantly via exit(-1) – see read_rules()’s docstring, same underlying PhysiCell behavior.

physicellpy.set_hypothesis_parameters(cell_type: str, signal: str, behavior: str, half_max: float, hill_power: float) → None

Set an existing rule’s Hill-function half_max/hill_power for the given (cell_type, signal, behavior) triple.

physicellpy.set_behavior_parameters(cell_type: str, behavior: str, min_value: float, base_or_max_value: object, max_value: object = None) → None

Set a behavior’s (min_value, max_value) – 3 args – or (min_value, base_value, max_value) – 4 args, pass max_value too.

physicellpy.set_behavior_base_value(cell_type: str, behavior: str, base_value: float) → None

Set only a behavior’s base_value (its value with every signal at its unstimulated level), leaving min_value/max_value untouched.

physicellpy.set_behavior_min_value(cell_type: str, behavior: str, min_value: float) → None

Set only a behavior’s min_value (the lower bound it saturates toward under a ‘decreases’ response), leaving base_value/max_value untouched.

physicellpy.set_behavior_max_value(cell_type: str, behavior: str, max_value: float) → None

Set only a behavior’s max_value (the upper bound it saturates toward under an ‘increases’ response), leaving base_value/min_value untouched.

physicellpy.get_single_signal(arg0: physicellpy.Cell, arg1: str) → float

Read a named signal’s current value for this cell, e.g. get_single_signal(cell, ‘custom:oncoprotein’) or get_single_signal(cell, ‘dead’).

physicellpy.get_single_behavior(arg0: physicellpy.Cell, arg1: str) → float

Read a named behavior’s current parameter value for this cell, e.g. get_single_behavior(cell, ‘cycle entry’) (the phase-0-to-phase-1 transition rate).

physicellpy.set_single_behavior(arg0: physicellpy.Cell, arg1: str, arg2: float) → None

Set a named behavior’s parameter value for this cell, e.g. set_single_behavior(cell, ‘cycle entry’, rate) or set_single_behavior(cell, ‘custom:oncoprotein’, p) (writes cell.custom_data[‘oncoprotein’]).

physicellpy.update_cell_and_death_parameters_O2_based(arg0: physicellpy.Cell, arg1: physicellpy.Phenotype, arg2: float) → None

PhysiCell’s standard O2-based update: sets necrosis/apoptosis rates and cycle-entry rate from the cell’s local oxygen signal. Most sample projects’ update_phenotype hooks call this first, then layer custom logic on top – same pattern as tumor_cell_phenotype_with_oncoprotein() in the heterogeneity sample project.

class physicellpy.HypothesisRule
add_signal(self: physicellpy.HypothesisRule, signal: str, half_max: float, hill_power: float, response: str) → None

Add a new Hill-function signal to this rule, e.g. rule.add_signal(‘oxygen’, 10, 4, ‘decreases’). response is ‘increases’ or ‘decreases’.

property applies_to_dead_cells

whether this signal is still evaluated once the cell is dead, parallel to signals

Type:

Per-signal flag

apply(self: physicellpy.HypothesisRule, arg0: physicellpy.Cell) → None

Evaluate and immediately write the result into the cell’s behavior (same as what happens automatically once per rules update).

property base_value

This behavior’s value when every signal this rule tracks is at its unstimulated (zero) level

property behavior

Name of the behavior this rule controls, e.g. ‘cycle entry’ or ‘apoptosis’ (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf’s behavior dictionary)

property cell_type

Name of the cell type this rule applies to

evaluate(self: physicellpy.HypothesisRule, arg0: physicellpy.Cell) → float

Evaluate this rule’s current Hill-function response for a live cell (reads its own signal values) – does not apply/write anything.

find_signal(self: physicellpy.HypothesisRule, arg0: str) → int

Index of the given signal name in signals/half_maxes/hill_powers/… (-1 if this rule doesn’t respond to that signal).

property half_maxes

Per-signal Hill half-max (the signal value giving a half-maximal response), parallel to signals

property hill_powers

Per-signal Hill exponent (steepness of the response curve), parallel to signals

property max_value

Upper bound the behavior saturates toward under an ‘increases’ response

property min_value

Lower bound the behavior saturates toward under a ‘decreases’ response

property responses

Per-signal response direction, ‘increases’ or ‘decreases’, parallel to signals

set_half_max(self: physicellpy.HypothesisRule, signal: str, half_max: float) → None

Set the Hill half-max for an existing signal on this rule

set_hill_power(self: physicellpy.HypothesisRule, signal: str, hill_power: float) → None

Set the Hill exponent for an existing signal on this rule (PhysiCell rounds this to the nearest integer)

set_response(self: physicellpy.HypothesisRule, signal: str, response: str) → None

Set whether an existing signal ‘increases’ or ‘decreases’ this rule’s behavior

property signals

Names of every signal this rule responds to, e.g. ‘oxygen’ or ‘contact with zombie’ (Cell_grammar_supp.pdf’s signal dictionary); parallel to responses/half_maxes/hill_powers/applies_to_dead_cells

find_behavior(self: physicellpy.HypothesisRuleset, arg0: str) → physicellpy.HypothesisRule

The HypothesisRule governing this behavior for this cell type, or None if no rule targets it.

Output

physicellpy.save_svg(filename: str, cell_coloring: str = 'by_number', z_slice: float = 0.0) → None

Write an SVG cross-section snapshot (cells over a substrate density colormap) at the current simulation time. cell_coloring picks one of PhysiCell’s built-in schemes – ‘by_number’ (default, colors by cell type), ‘live_dead’, ‘simple’, ‘cytometry’, ‘ki67’, ‘cycling_quiescent’, ‘hematoxylin_eosin’ – or ‘custom’ to use whatever function was last passed to set_svg_coloring_function(). Set pc.svg_options.length_bar etc. beforehand to match main.cpp’s PhysiCell_SVG_options.length_bar = 200 convention.

physicellpy.save_svg_legend(filename: str, cell_coloring: str = 'by_number') → None

Write an SVG legend for the given cell_coloring scheme (see save_svg()), listing every registered cell type’s color.

physicellpy.save_multicellds(filename_base: str) → None

Write a MultiCellDS v2 snapshot (XML index + MATLAB .mat mesh/microenvironment/cell files) at the current simulation time. filename_base has no extension – PhysiCell appends its own, e.g. pc.save_multicellds(pc.config_folder() + ‘/output00000001’).

physicellpy.set_svg_coloring_function(cell_coloring_function: Callable) → None

Register a Python callable cell_coloring_function(cell) -> [fill, outline, nucleus_fill, nucleus_outline] (exactly 4 color strings, e.g. ‘rgb(255,0,0)’ or ‘black’) as a custom SVG coloring scheme – the same 4-string convention PhysiCell’s own built-in coloring functions return. Pass cell_coloring=’custom’ to save_svg()/save_svg_legend() to use it. Only one custom function can be registered at a time; calling this again replaces it. If the function raises, or returns something other than 4 strings, that cell falls back to ‘by_number’ coloring for that one call rather than aborting the snapshot.

physicellpy.clear_svg_coloring_function() → None

Unregister the function set by set_svg_coloring_function(). cell_coloring=’custom’ will raise until a new one is registered.

class physicellpy.SVGOptions

PhysiMeSS (fibre agents)

physicellpy.setup_physimess_cell_definition(cell_definition: physicellpy.CellDefinition, is_fibre: bool = False) → None

Wire a CellDefinition up for PhysiMeSS – equivalent to the handful of cd->functions.xxx = … lines every PhysiMeSS sample project’s own create_cell_types() writes by hand. is_fibre=True makes create_cell() construct a PhysiMeSSFibre (mechanically a rigid rod) instead of a PhysiMeSSCell for this type – call is_fibre()/fibre_cell_definitions() to decide which, matching the name-based convention every PhysiMeSS config already relies on. Call this on every registered CellDefinition (pc.cell_defaults included) before creating any cells of that type – instantiate_cell is read once, at create_cell() time.

physicellpy.is_fibre(arg0: object) → bool

True if this Cell or CellDefinition is a fibre type – decided purely by name (case-sensitive substring match on ‘ecm’, ‘matrix’, ‘fiber’, ‘fibre’, or ‘rod’; see PhysiMeSS_fibre.cpp). No separate registration step exists – naming a CellDefinition ‘ecm’ (etc.) in your XML is what makes it a fibre type.

physicellpy.fibre_cell_definitions() → list[physicellpy.CellDefinition]

Every currently-registered CellDefinition that is_fibre() considers a fibre type.

physicellpy.physimess_mechanics(dt: float) → None

Advance fibre-fibre/cell-fibre neighbor tracking and crosslinking. Self-gates on a static last-update-time (same pattern Cell_Container::update_all_cells uses internally), so it’s safe to call unconditionally every diffusion step – matches main.cpp’s own call site exactly: pc.physimess_mechanics(pc.mechanics_dt()) right before pc.run_simulation_step().

physicellpy.remove_physimess_out_of_bounds_fibres() → None

Delete any fibre still out-of-bounds after check_out_of_bounds()’s re-roll attempts were exhausted. Call once after placing all fibres during setup, matching every PhysiMeSS sample project’s own setup_tissue().

class physicellpy.PhysiMeSSFibre
assign_fibre_orientation(self: physicellpy.PhysiMeSSFibre) → None

Set length/radius from this cell’s own custom_data (‘fibre_length’, ‘length_normdist_sd’, ‘fibre_radius’) and pick an orientation (random, or from ‘fibre_angle’/’angle_normdist_sd’ if custom_data[‘anisotropic_fibres’] is set). Call once right after create_cell()+assign_position() for a fibre, matching every PhysiMeSS sample project’s own setup_tissue().

check_out_of_bounds(self: physicellpy.PhysiMeSSFibre, position: list[float]) → None

Re-roll this fibre’s orientation (up to 10 attempts) if its endpoints – computed from position +/- length*orientation – fall outside the domain. Call after assign_fibre_orientation(); remove_physimess_out_of_bounds_fibres() removes anything that still fails after this.

property crosslink_count

Number of other fibres this fibre is currently crosslinked to

property length

Fibre length (micron), set by assign_fibre_orientation()

property radius

Fibre (cylinder) radius (micron), set by assign_fibre_orientation()

class physicellpy.PhysiMeSSCell
property stuck_counter

Consecutive steps this cell has been mechanically stuck against a fibre

property unstuck_counter

Consecutive steps since this cell last broke free from a fibre
